items.title: Ukrainian photographer Vic Bakin captures the traces of war left on the bodies and landscapes left behind
items.description: In February 2022, when Russian troops launched their invasion of Ukraine, Vic Bakin decided to keep a photographic journal of the unfolding conflict. His images, highly personal and sometimes altered, mixed with portraits of Ukrainian youth, make up the series 'Epitome,' which has received several awards since.

items.title: Ukrainian soldiers march in Kyiv's Pride parade to push for equal rights
items.description: Ukrainian soldiers and their partners march in Kyiv's Pride parade for the right to marry and enter into civil partnerships in a traditional country that's trying to modernize as it aligns with Western Europe.

items.title: Vance meets top Iranian officials as US looks to get negotiations back on track
items.description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance and top Iranian officials are trying to build out the interim deal to end the war in Iran reached by the two sides last week. They are meeting at a Swiss mountainside resort near Lake Lucerne.

items.title: Are Ukraine drones really exposing gaps in Russia's defense?
items.description: Once seen as almost impenetrable, Russian air defenses are now under growing strain from Ukrainian drones. A recent attack on Moscow has reignited debate over Russian vulnerabilities.

items.title: Sudan: Security Council warns of mass atrocity risk in El Obeid
items.description: The UN Security Council has expressed alarm over reports of substantial military reinforcements by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) around El Obeid in Sudan, warning of the risk of a potential ground offensive on the city.
